title: OpenAI says ChatGPT Ads hit a $1 billion annualized run rate in 200 days
subtitle: The advertising business OpenAI launched inside ChatGPT in the U.S. earlier this year has scaled faster than any other line the company has tracked publicly, and it is now open to marketers in more than 40 countries.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI told reporters on August 31 that ChatGPT Ads has reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate roughly 200 days after its U.S. launch. The company also opened its self-serve ad platform to marketers in India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa the same day, bringing the total footprint to more than 40 countries. OpenAI still projects $2.5 billion in ad revenue by the end of 2026 and a total annualized revenue line exceeding $40 billion. In April, the company had said the ads pilot crossed $100 million in annualized revenue within six weeks of launch — the run rate has grown roughly tenfold since.

The number is significant because until this year, the story on OpenAI's economics was almost entirely subscription revenue plus API usage, both bounded by how many people or apps pay for the model. Ads are a different curve: they scale with time-on-surface, not seat count, and they turn every free ChatGPT session into inventory. Hitting a billion-dollar run rate in 200 days is the first hard evidence that a general-purpose chatbot can carry an ad load without collapsing the user experience — or at least without collapsing it fast enough to show up in the growth numbers.

The timing lines up with OpenAI's IPO groundwork. A company preparing for a public listing needs a revenue mix that public markets can model, and a single line — enterprise contracts — is not enough on its own. Advertising gives OpenAI what Google had at its own IPO: a scalable, high-margin second pillar that grows with usage. It also puts OpenAI into direct commercial conflict with Google in a way that model quality alone never quite did, since both companies now sell attention on a conversational surface.

Takeaway for learners: when a product you use free-of-charge starts monetizing through ads, the incentive structure shifts underneath you — even if the interface looks identical. Watch for subtle changes: which sources the model cites, when it suggests a specific brand, how it phrases product comparisons. Building the habit of asking 'who is paying for this answer' is a media-literacy skill worth carrying into every AI tool you use, not just ChatGPT.
